answer: At a river jetty, a co-op hires agents to cut delays for a ferry with opal trim. Each timetable is bonded and tested on an assigned shift against a published baseline. The exchange pays for minutes saved, not accounts, and groups plans with identical boat assignments into one fee. Fifty fake names replaying one plan still earn one fee. To win fifty, an attacker must devise fifty workable improvements and risk fifty bonds if logs contradict passenger scans. Dispatchers could fabricate delays, so auditors compare ticket times with engine records before settlement.
